issues.issue: Does Guideline 7, by requiring claimants to be questioned first by the RPO or member, breach their s. 7 Charter right to participate, i.e. to be questioned first by their own counsel?
issues.applicant_position: Guideline 7 denies claimants the right to be questioned first by their own counsel, contrary to fundamental justice under s. 7.
issues.result_quote: it is my opinion that Guideline 7 does not violate claimants’ right to participate at an RPD hearing conducted in accordance with the principles of fundamental justice

issues.issue: Does Guideline 7 breach s. 7 by creating a reasonable apprehension of bias or lack of independence of RPD members?
issues.applicant_position: Members questioning claimants first are drawn into the fray, creating a reasonable apprehension of bias contrary to s. 7.
issues.result_quote: I would conclude that Guideline 7 does not infringe section 7 of the Charter by creating a reasonable apprehension of bias

issues.issue: Is Guideline 7 an unlawful fetter on RPD members’ discretion, or ultra vires the Chairperson’s guideline-making power under paragraph 159(1)(h) of IRPA?
issues.applicant_position: Guideline 7 unlawfully fetters RPD members’ discretion and exceeds the Chairperson’s guideline power.
issues.result_quote: Nor is it is an unlawful fetter on members’ discretion, and it was not legally required to have been issued under the Chairperson’s statutory power

issues.issue: Must a finding that Guideline 7 fetters discretion mean the judicial review is granted (certified Q4), and when must an objection to Guideline 7 be raised (certified Q7)?
issues.result_quote: It is not necessary to answer this question.

issues.issue: Should costs be awarded for special reasons in these applications and appeals under Rule 22?
issues.applicant_position: Costs were specifically requested in only two appellate memoranda; grounds not stated.
issues.result_quote: In my opinion, “special reasons” do not exist in this case.

issues.issue: Did the RPD unreasonably find Mr. Benitez not credible, so that the Federal Court erred in dismissing his judicial review?
issues.applicant_position: Says the RPD’s non-credibility finding should be set aside.
issues.result_quote: there is no basis for disturbing Justice Gibson’s decision

issues.issue: Were the RPD’s findings of fact in the Guirguis claim unreasonable, so that the Federal Court erred in dismissing their judicial review?
issues.applicant_position: Asks the court to substitute its view of the evidence for the RPD’s findings.
issues.result_quote: This is not the role either of the Federal Court on an application for judicial review, or of this Court

issues.issue: May Ms. Gyankoma raise non-Guideline 7 issues for the first time on appeal?
issues.applicant_position: Wishes to raise several non-Guideline 7 issues not argued in the Federal Court.
issues.result_quote: No comparable reasons exist in the present case for permitting counsel to raise non-Guideline 7 issues for the first time in this Court

issues.issue: Did the RPD unreasonably find Mr. Matheen’s claim fabricated, so that the Federal Court erred in dismissing his judicial review?
issues.applicant_position: Challenges the RPD’s finding that his claim was fabricated; submissions not summarized.
issues.result_quote: I see no reason for interfering with Justice Gibson’s decision, and would dismiss the appeal.
